speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are here because of a generalized rash on your newborn. Can you tell me when the rash first appeared and if it has spread or changed since birth?

speaker: Patient
text: 4-day-old newborn. The newborn was born at term with no complications. The mother had no prenatal care and has a history of gonorrhea treated 4 years ago. The newborn presents with a generalized rash that has been present for 1 day.

speaker: Doctor
text: Did the infant experience any fever, irritability, or feeding difficulties, and are there any lesions on the palms, soles, or mucous membranes? I need to check for signs of systemic involvement or specific distribution patterns.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Generalized erythematous maculopapular rash and pustules. I also have Rash with an erythematous base, Rash over the trunk and extremities, Sparing of the palms and soles.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the lack of prenatal care and the rash sparing the palms and soles, I am concerned about early congenital syphilis despite the atypical presentation. REQUEST TEST: Darkfield microscopy of lesion fluid, VDRL/RPR, and PCR for Treponema pallidum.

speaker: Doctor
text: Since congenital syphilis has been ruled out and the palms and soles are spared, this presentation is highly suggestive of erythema toxicum neonatorum. I will perform a physical exam to confirm the presence of central pustules on an erythematous base and check for any other systemic signs of infection.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Born at term, no prenatal care for the mother, mother's history of gonorrhea treated 4 years ago. Social history: N/A for the newborn.

speaker: Doctor
text: Does the infant appear well-appearing, afebrile, and feeding normally, with no other systemic symptoms? I need to confirm the benign nature of this rash before proceeding.

speaker: Patient
text: No other abnormalities noted in the systems review; the rest of the examination shows no abnormalities.

speaker: Doctor
text: The infant is well-appearing with a benign rash sparing the palms and soles, which is classic for erythema toxicum neonatorum. DIAGNOSIS READY: Erythema toxicum neonatorum
